messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: hosted-runtime/kvcache-prefetch-controller memory spike detected. 90th percentile kv-map size increased 6x over baseline. Errors: OOMs on 3 GPUs in pod group runtime-hosted-3. Pager: sre-oncall-jess. Link: https://telemetry/redwood/alerts/1765432100

sre-oncall-jess: I'm on it. Gathering context — is this correlated with any rollout or prefetch config changes in the last 30m?

prashant: I'm seeing a deployment roll forward to runtime-hosted:v1.4.0 ~12m ago that included prefetch controller tuning (aggressive lookahead). Could be the new prefetch window + no TTL for kvcache entries.

runtime-eng-lee: Confirmed. We pushed the prefetch window increase to 8k tokens for high-throughput models. Also enabled continuous batching change that merges over longer windows.

maria-product: Heads-up — several customers reported higher latencies ~5-10s and some 500s for long-prompt workloads. Already notified a couple of account teams.

kyle-cust-ops: We have a support ticket from 2 enterprise customers complaining about timed-out streaming responses. We need ETA on mitigation to update them.

prashant: Immediate mitigation plan: 1) pause prefetch controller for hosted runtime, 2) reduce batching window to previous value, 3) force kv entry TTL (evict long tails). Will coordinate rollback if needed.

sre-oncall-jess: Go for pause. Prashant — do the commands and post the exact steps here so we can audit. I'll notify SEs and CS to throttle new sessions that might trigger long context.

runtime-eng-lee: Doing step 1 now — pausing prefetch controller on runtime-hosted namespace. CLI:```kubectl -n hosted-runtime scale deployment kvcache-prefetch-controller --replicas=0```

prashant: Applied. Prefetch controller replicas -> 0. Telemetry shows prefetch traffic dropping immediately.

incident-bot: system: Prefetch QPS dropped 87% in 60s. Memory growth rate reduced but KV map still large due to existing entries.

runtime-eng-lee: Next, applying TTL policy to kvmap to expire entries > 24h and aggressive eviction for entries > 500k tok. Patch:```PATCH /runtime-hosted/config
{
  "kv_ttl_seconds": 86400,
  "eviction_threshold_tokens": 500000
}
```

prashant: Patch applied as a runtime feature flag (kvcache_ttl:v2). Eviction job queued. Expect progressive reduction over 2-10 minutes.

maria-product: Can we also throttle new long-prompt sessions at the edge? We want to avoid more growth while eviction ramps.

runtime-eng-lee: Yes — setting a short-circuit on API gateway for requests with prompt_len > 50k tokens to return 413/slow-path. Command:```curl -X POST https://edge-config/set -d '{"long_prompt_rejection": {"enabled": true, "max_tokens": 50000}}'```

kyle-cust-ops: Notifying customers now: holding message "We're actively mitigating a runtime memory regression affecting long-prompt performance; short-term workarounds include reducing prompt length or switching to dedicated capacity."

incident-bot: annotation: On-call handoff scheduled — SRE leads prashant and runtime-eng-lee. Pager acknowledged by prashant at 1765432160.

sre-oncall-jess: I'm handing off — need to sleep. prashant/lee take lead, I'll be reachable for escalation.

prashant: Taking lead. Next step: if eviction doesn't reduce memory within 10m, initiate rollback of v1.4.0 -> v1.3.9 runtime image to remove prefetch/continuous-batching changes. Rollback command (requires approval):```rbctl rollback --service runtime-hosted --to v1.3.9 --reason "kvcache runaway context spike"```

runtime-eng-lee: Running memory heap diffs and sampling user sessions to identify offending prefixes. Early indicator: 70% of the new kv entries are from a small set of sessions that do repeated token-prefix generation (prefix amplification).

prashant: We should also enable immediate throttling on background prefetch jobs to 1% of original QPS as an extra safeguard. Applying:```kubectl -n hosted-runtime set env deployment kvcache-prefetch-workers PREFETCH_RATE=0.01```

incident-bot: system: Prefetch workers env updated. Prefetch job run-rate down to ~0.8% of prior baseline. Memory allocation delta trending down.

maria-product: Customer impact summary so far: ~8-12% of hosted API calls for long-prompt customers experienced >3s latency and ~0.3% observed 5xx increases during spike window. No customer data loss. Will prepare an incident email once we have final numbers.

kyle-cust-ops: Customer comms drafted and queued for send-after-mitigation.

prashant: Eviction job reports: evicted 62% of large entries over the last 6m. Host memory per pod reduced from 78% to 42% on the worst nodes. OOMs have ceased for the last 3 minutes.

runtime-eng-lee: Given current telemetry, rollback not required. We'll keep prefetch paused and the TTL patch in place. Schedule a hotfix release that reintroduces prefetch with conservative defaults + unit tests for prefix-amplification.

sre-oncall-jess: Thanks team. I'm back on rotation but leaving the thread open for 1hr post-closure. Prashant — please create a followup postmortem doc with timeline and root cause.

prashant: Will do. Tentative RCA: prefetch window bump + continuous-batching merge created a pathological prefix amplification loop for long prompts, ending in kvmap growth + memory exhaustion. Immediate mitigations: pause prefetch, apply TTL + eviction, throttle prefetch jobs, edge long-prompt throttling, communicate with customers. Next actions: rollout hotfix with conservative prefetch heuristics, add guardrails (max entries per session), and automated alert for kvmap growth rate > x tokens/min.

incident-bot: incident closed to paging. Severity downgraded to SEV2 at 1765432500. Postmortem owner: prashant.

maria-product: Thanks all. I'll coordinate the customer followups and product notes. :thumbsup:
